name: Opus-fleet deep value
strategy: Concentrated in sub-market-multiple, FCF-rich dividend payers (banks below book, energy, pharma, telecom, staples) with a small hedge shorting the most stretched growth cohort.

positions.thesis: Raised 20% -> 22% and now the top weight, because the single objection I had against it was answered this week by the market rather than by me. I held it at 20% saying the $28.61 consensus visibly had not been refreshed for raised FY26 guidance, the productivity savings, or the CEO's $1m open-market purchase. It has now refreshed to $32.36 - a 13% jump in the target - after FDA approval of the XFG-adapted COVID vaccine on 27 Aug, a $500m raise to the FY26 revenue midpoint to $61.5bn with adj. EPS held at $2.80-3.00, and 28 Aug pipeline updates across obesity, oncology and autoimmune. At $28.07 that is 15.3% of upside on 10.13x forward against a roughly 19x industry, with a 6.1% yield and 28 analysts at Buy. The structural reason matters more this week than last: it is the only holding with no crude beta, no AI-capex duration and no consumer-credit cyclicality, and I have just watched both of my macro drivers reverse inside five sessions. That is precisely when the leg that answers to neither of them earns more weight, not less. The honest negative is sharper now, not softer: a 6% yield competes against a 30-year at 5.21% with a Fed chair floating hikes, so the carry argument is weak. I own it for the multiple and the pipeline, and it is trading at a 52-week high because the pipeline delivered. Stop stays wide at -18% so a multi-year re-rating is never converted into a stop-out by one session.

Cut 22% -> 18% by my own arithmetic, not by a change of mind. One week ago I raised this from 16% to 22% and stated the reason in one sentence: 16% was the weight justified by Brent at $88-90, and Brent was $94.39. Brent is now $88.50-90.07 after Iran and Oman agreed a Hormuz revenue-sharing framework and flows began improving. The condition I named is gone, so the weight I attached to it goes with it - anything else makes the sizing rule a one-way ratchet that only ever adds. I do not go all the way back to 16% for two reasons I can defend on numbers. First, the physical market is materially tighter than when 16% was set: the IEA now models a Q3-26 deficit of 1.8 mb/d, more than double last month's ~0.8 mb/d, with 2026 supply down 4.3 mb/d, so the same headline crude price sits on a much thinner cushion. Second, the equity told me something: CVX fell only about 1.7% while crude fell 5.1%, which is what beta 0.49 and a company leg of record $20.59bn quarterly net income, Permian and Hess volumes, record US refinery throughput and a 20-year Microsoft data-centre power contract look like. At $201.86 it is roughly 13x forward with a 3.5% yield and a $217.88 consensus implying about 8% upside. It stays the book's inflation hedge, which is not a small job in a week when the Fed chair said his job on inflation is not done. I keep the stop at -15% rather than loosening it back out with the smaller size, because the driver is now actively unwinding rather than confirming, and that raises the odds of the drawdown the stop exists for.

Held flat at 14% with the tension stated rather than smoothed over, because this is the one leg where the week's news genuinely cut both ways and I will not manufacture a decision to look decisive. Against me, and I have to own it: the rate mechanism I underwrote was long-end-led steepening, and what actually happened was front-end-led flattening - the 2y jumped 12bp to 4.356% on Warsh while the 30y moved 2bp to 5.211%. That is not my thesis, and a Fed hiking into a labour market with negative payrolls and 103k of downward revisions is a live credit risk for a bank whose US Personal Banking and cards book is consumer-levered. August card data was mixed in exactly that shape: charge-offs up, though delinquencies - the leading half - actually declined. For me: the discount has not closed at all. $132.90 is 11.38x forward with a $154.50 consensus from 21 analysts implying 16.3% upside, still the cheapest large-cap US bank, on 2025 revenue of $75.7bn up 6.7% with earnings up 13.6%, and the whole curve sitting at high absolute levels supports deposit spread even when its shape is wrong for me. There is a book-level reason too: I just cut oil exposure from 28% to 18% of NAV, and this leg was the internal hedge against that shock, so it is doing less hedging work and more standalone-value work now. What I will not do is add. My own correction stands - at about 1.34x tangible book there is no buyback-accretion kicker, and my mandate's 'banks below book' line is not what this is. Stop stays at -20%; I said a value thesis in a volatile rate debate needs room and I am not tightening it the first week the debate goes against me.

Raised 7% -> 9%, because the specific test I wrote down two weeks ago was passed in the strongest form it could be passed. My rule was: do not add to this short unless the tape accepts the de-rating mechanism, since adding to a losing short on a thesis the market has just refused is how a hedge becomes a bet. This week the tape did more than accept it. NVIDIA beat and jumped roughly 7-9% on Thursday, SMH rallied 3.5% intraday, industry capex forecasts were raised ABOVE $1trn for 2026 with hyperscalers at about $815bn and 111% growth - and the cohort still closed the week down about 3%, with Marvell -10% on gross-margin guidance and Applied Materials -5%. Fundamentals accelerated and the group fell anyway. Good news failing to lift a cohort is the cleanest confirmation a short gets, and it is a different and better signal than the price drop alone. The discount-rate mechanism also escalated: Warsh said the Fed still has work to do on inflation and traders moved to price a possible September hike, which is a direct multiple headwind for the longest-duration equity in the market. Valuation is unchanged and is the most stretched cohort available, which is what the mandate asks of the hedge: 44.89x, NVIDIA at 21.70% of the fund, top ten at 71.46%, beta 1.74, after a 94.6% twelve-month total return. The honest risk is that capex up 111% can squeeze this violently, which is why it is sized for survival and not for a view: 9% with a -22% stop risks about 2% of the book, and 3% borrow costs roughly 27bp a year. The +30% take-profit stays - this is insurance, and I bank it if a real de-rating arrives rather than let it round-trip.

Cut 11% -> 5%, completing the retreat I began two weeks ago, because both stated reasons to own it have now been used up rather than merely weakened. The valuation reason is finished on my own threshold: I wrote that a deep-value book should not pay a full weight for a 4.3% gap to consensus, and at $50.10 against a $51.56 target from 26 analysts the gap is 2.9%. I cannot apply that sentence to justify a trim at 4.3% and then ignore it at 2.9%. The risk reason got worse again in the way I flagged: SpaceX has confirmed Starlink Mobile launching in 2027, and it is now the named investor concern on the stock rather than a hypothetical about terminal value. And the macro turned hostile in a third, new way - a Fed chair openly discussing hikes with the 30-year at 5.211% is the worst available regime for a 5.7% yielder, and that is the argument that retired MO. What keeps a residual 5% instead of zero is that the operating leg keeps beating and the stock keeps RISING while its rate proxy sells off, which says the market is paying for the company and not the coupon: 184,000 postpaid adds, raised full-year revenue and free-cash-flow guidance, a $4.5bn buyback target, the $1bn+ Google dark-fiber deal that makes the AI buildout pay Verizon rent, and NetSense with Lockheed and NVIDIA. At 9.75x forward with beta 0.24 it is still cheap low-beta carry - it just no longer deserves a conviction weight. I tighten the stop from -15% to -12% to match that demotion: a residual position held on execution rather than on a valuation gap should not be given the room a conviction thesis gets.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-29: Three pre-committed rules fired at once, and the whole value of writing rules down is that I execute them when they cut against me. (1) I raised CVX 16% -> 22% one week ago on one explicit number - Brent $94.39 - having stated in writing that 16% was the weight justified by Brent at $88-90. Brent is $88.50-90.07. If I only ever add when the driver confirms and never subtract when it reverses, the sizing arithmetic is decoration, so CVX comes down. It goes to 18% rather than back to 16% because the physical balance is genuinely tighter than when I set 16% (IEA Q3 deficit doubled to 1.8 mb/d) and because CVX fell only 1.7% against crude -5.1%, which says the equity is not a pure crude proxy. (2) VLO: my rule is that once a name trades past consensus the specific dislocation is harvested. It is now 11.7% above target at an all-time high, refining margins peaked in mid-July and are falling, and the crude leg of the crack is de-escalating. I kept 6% last week on the cheap multiple; with the driver now reversing there is nothing left to wait for, so I take the profit rather than let a mean-reverting cash flow capitalised at a peak round-trip. (3) VZ: I wrote that a deep-value book should not pay a full weight for a 4.3% gap to consensus. The gap is now 2.9%, Starlink Mobile is confirmed for 2027, and a Fed openly discussing hikes is the worst regime for a 5.7% yielder. It goes to a residual 5%. The two adds are the mirror image of the same discipline: PFE 20% -> 22% because the one thing I said was missing actually happened - consensus re-rated $28.61 -> $32.36 on the XFG approval, the raised FY26 guide and the pipeline updates, so my 'stale target' argument was proven rather than merely asserted; and SMH short 7% -> 9% because I set an explicit test last week (I refuse to add to this short unless the tape accepts the mechanism) and the tape passed it in the strongest available form - NVDA beat, capex forecasts went ABOVE $1trn, and the cohort still fell ~3% on the week - while Warsh signalling possible hikes escalates the exact discount-rate transmission I am short. The residual goes to cash, not to a new name: I screened BMY (zero upside to consensus) and MRK (0.26%) and the sub-book banks are all micro-cap, and in a deep-value mandate 'nothing is cheap enough' is a real answer. 32% cash earning 4% is also the option to re-buy CVX if Hormuz re-escalates, which this series has done twice since July.
novelty: I manage no Round-2 book, so the cross-round overlap constraint does not bind; this is my only book.
research_notes:
CHECKED THIS WEEK (prices through 2026-08-28 close):

MACRO 1 — the oil premium unwound. Brent went $94.39 -> roughly $88.50-90.07, about -5.1% on the week, after Iran and Oman agreed a Strait of Hormuz revenue-sharing framework and Hormuz flows began improving. Tehran says this is not an immediate reopening and the Trump administration says it will not return to the collapsed June terms, so the standoff is live, but the tape has taken a real bite out of the risk premium. Context on how violent this series is: Brent printed $69 on 2 July, $105 on 23 July, $94 last week, $88-90 now. Offsetting: the IEA August report now shows a Q3-26 deficit of 1.8 mb/d, more than double last month's ~0.8 mb/d, with 2026 supply falling 4.3 mb/d; EIA has Brent averaging ~$85 in Q3. So the physical balance is tighter than when I last sized CVX for $88-90 crude, even though the price is back there.

MACRO 2 — the Fed turned hawkish in a way that changes the discount rate. Warsh at Jackson Hole said the Fed still has "work to do" and that better summer PCE/CPI prints "do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved"; traders moved to price a possible HIKE as soon as September. 2y +12bp to 4.356%, 10y 4.726%, 30y 5.211%. Front-end-led, so the curve flattened rather than steepened - that is not the mechanism I underwrote for C, and it is a stagflationary setup (hiking into a labour market that printed negative payrolls with 103k of downward revisions).

POSITIONS:
- CVX $201.86 (+1.05% Fri). Down only ~1.7% on the week against crude -5.1%, i.e. the equity absorbed far less than the commodity - record earnings, Permian/Hess volumes, the 20-year Microsoft power deal and beta 0.49 are carrying it.
- PFE $28.07, essentially at its 52-week high of $28.44, +15.1% in a month, +18.6% YTD. The consensus target I complained was stale has now refreshed hard: $28.61 -> $32.36, about 15% upside. FDA approved the Pfizer/BioNTech XFG-adapted COVID vaccine on 27 Aug; FY26 revenue guidance midpoint raised $500m to $61.5bn with adj. EPS $2.80-3.00 held; 28 Aug pipeline updates across obesity, oncology and autoimmune. My "consensus has not been refreshed" thesis was validated, upward.
- C $132.90, 11.38x forward, $154.50 target from 21 analysts (+16.25%), 52-week range $92.96-$147.96. August card data: delinquencies DOWN, charge-offs UP. Commentary flags elevated borrowing costs pressuring consumer credit quality.
- VZ $50.10 vs a $51.56 consensus - only 2.9% of upside left. SpaceX confirmed Starlink Mobile launching 2027 and it is now the named investor concern on the stock.
- SMH ~$553.12 (VanEck NAV) vs $560.42 last week and my $569.41 entry, about -3% on the week. The important part is HOW: NVDA beat and jumped ~7-9% on Thursday, SMH rallied 3.5% intraday, and the cohort still finished the week down, with Marvell -10% on gross-margin guidance and AMAT -5%. Rolland raised 2026 industry capex above $1trn (hyperscalers ~$815bn, +111% y/y) - so fundamentals accelerated and the cohort fell anyway. Good news failing to lift the group is the strongest confirmation my de-rating mechanism gets, and Warsh escalates it.
- VLO ~$349 (ATH $353.00 set 24 Aug), +84.7% YTD, now 11.7% ABOVE its $312.53 consensus. US refining margins peaked mid-July and have been falling since.

SCREENED FOR REPLACEMENTS, FOUND NOTHING: BMY 10.2-10.5x forward and 3.86% yield but at ~$65.3 against a $65.4-66.2 consensus - zero upside, 18 Holds. MRK $148.28 against a $148.73 target - 0.26% upside. Large-cap banks below tangible book: the sub-1x names are community/small regionals (0.4-0.7x TBV), not investable size for this book; USB is 2.30x TBV. I am not manufacturing a position to spend cash.
